events.what: An internal research version of Claude produces a proof that more than 67.2% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line (up from about 41.7%); verified by Alpöge and Furman
events.ai_basis: A proof of these results was very recently produced by an internal research version of Claude developed by Anthropic and subsequently verified by Alpöge and Furman.

events.what: Lamzouri gives an independent human proof of the same >2/3 bound (>67.25% simple and on the line), crediting Claude's earlier result
Various preprints claiming full proofs or disproofs of RH (e.g. arXiv:2404.06306 in math.GM, a Zenodo 'most definitive disproof')
events.credibility_reason: Landmark problem, no expert uptake, math.GM / Zenodo venues, repeated revisions; later work (Lamzouri, Anthropic) treats RH as open.

judgement.doubts: The bullet is the yes/no RH question; a proportion-of-zeros lower bound is a bound on a quantity whose value 100% is RH-adjacent, so `progress` is the right tier. Lamzouri's later human proof reproduces the same bound with a slightly higher constant; I treat it as a reproduction that confirms rather than supersedes the AI result (its title calls it 'a new proof'), so the AI role stays with the Claude event. Had Lamzouri's marginal improvement been counted as superseding, ai_role would be none. Verification of the Claude result by external experts Conrey and Goldston rests on secondary reporting only; Alpöge and Furman are Anthropic staff, but Lamzouri's independent proof is strong confirmation.

corrections.why: other: kept. The status rests on the Claude event ('A proof of these results was very recently produced by an internal research version of Claude ... verified by Alpöge and Furman'). Doubt: Lamzouri's later human paper (arXiv:2609.02882) proves a slightly larger constant (>67.25%); I read it as an independent reproduction crediting Claude, not a superseding bound under §4 step 3, but a stricter reader could make it the rests-on event with ai_role none.
